utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Ms. Merinda Stewart, appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Aleksandar Aleksic, appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything that need engage our attention before we revert to closed session? In which case [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Inasmuch as there's a possibility that the interpreters don't have copies of these two rulings, I'm going to pace myself in the delivery of them. On the 14th of July, 2010, the Prosecution filed its motion to amend its Rule 65 ter witness list by adding Witness ST-257 in which it seeks, first, to add ST-257 to its Rule 65 ter witness list and, secondly, to adduce ST-257's evidence, pursuant to Rule 92 ter. The Prosecution seeks to call ST-257 to testify on an attack on the village of Renovica. The Defence responded jointly on the 28th of July, 2010, opposing the motion, arguing that the Prosecution failed to exercise due diligence by neglecting to identify the best and most credible witness which it planned to rely upon. Considering that ST-257's evidence would be probative and necessary for the Prosecution to prove the attack on Renovica as alleged in its indictment and also considering that given the nature of 257's expected testimony, the Trial Chamber would prefer to hear 257 viva voce. The Trial Chamber grants the Prosecution leave to add ST-257 to its 65 ter witness list, orders that the Prosecution call 257 viva voce, and grants it 45 minutes for its examination-in-chief. Second ruling is as follows: On the 12th of October, 2010, the Trial Chamber granted the Prosecution leave to add ST-041 to its Rule 65 ter witness list, to respond to a Defence challenge to Adjudicated Fact 1268 arising from its cross-examination of witnesses ST-216, and ST-162. The Prosecution had proposed that ST-041 be heard pursuant to Rule 92 bis and the Trial Chamber ordered the Prosecution to file any such application within seven days of the date of the Chamber's decision. On the 19th of October, 2010, the Prosecution filed a motion submitting two statements from Witness ST-041 for admission pursuant to Rule 92 bis, highlighting in blue passages relevant to challenged Adjudicated Fact 1268, and highlighting in yellow contextual information relevant to those facts. The Stanisic Defence and the Zupljanin Defence filed a joint response on the 2nd of November, 2010, opposing the admission of the statement into evidence and requesting that the Trial Chamber order ST-041 to appear for cross-examination, asserting that the only means to confront the evidence and challenge the adjudicated fact is by cross-examination of ST-041. Citing its decision on the 12th of October, 2010, the Trial Chamber recalls that the Defence's cross-examination of ST-216 and ST-162 constituted a prima facie reliable and credible challenge to Adjudicated Fact 1268, pertaining to the discriminatory application of a curfew to non-Serbs in Doboj in May 1992. Considering that the challenge is limited to only the enforcement of the curfew and not the adjudicated fact, considering also that ST-041 is to testify to a fact on which the Trial Chamber has received conflicting evidence, the Trial Chamber, pursuant to Rule 92 bis(A)(ii)(C) denies the Prosecution's request to receive ST-041's evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis and instead grants the Prosecution leave to call ST-041 viva voce and grants the Prosecution 30 minutes for examination. The Prosecution's examination shall be limited to facts pertaining to enforcement of the curfew.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just inquire. I'm sorry. I completely misunderstood. We were given advance by Your Honours. I thought Your Honours ruling was going to be on all the 92 bis witnesses that we've applied to call for the adjudicated facts. And this -- this -- this -- clearly isn't. I'm simply asking -- I'm inquiring, Your Honours, again, for the purpose of arranging for future witnesses, when we are likely to get that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I know, Ms. Korner, that I'm beginning to sound like a broken record, but that is still being refined, and we fully expect to be in a position to deliver that finally tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Just for your information, to the Prosecution and to the Defence, the reason why the Chamber has taken its time to put together this decision on the 92 bis witnesses is that we wanted to wrap up all pending matters and try and see if it was possible to set out a time schedule for the remaining part of the Prosecution's case. So tomorrow will be the time when we will seek, and hopefully we will deliver our decision on the 92 bis witnesses and to the remaining pending issues on witnesses for which the Prosecution has filed motions, and also to the adjudicated fact witnesses, and to attempt to put out a closing date for the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment to tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 12th day of November, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
